reason: A keeps the logo → can → headline → CTA column clean and the can at a good size, but it shrinks the teal circle into a floating full circle that no longer bleeds off the edge, and the right green can dot nearly touches that circle. The bottom-left circle is also token-sized, and the legal line is tiny and pushed to the bottom. B keeps the circles big and bleeding like the original, but the GLACIER logo and the top of the can now sit on the teal circle. The fine print runs across the edge of the oversized bottom circle, and a dead band is left below it, so the bottom looks unresolved and the layout feels top-heavy.

A: the SOLSTICE logo is jammed against the top edge and sits right on the bottle cap. The body copy is tiny and hard to read at this size, and the bottle is pushed into the left corner, leaving a weak, sparse centre. B: the text is readable and the left-to-right order (logo, bottle, headline, CTA) is clear, but it is badly cramped. 'fizz' runs into the stacked decorative circles, the CTA and the three-line body copy nearly touch the bottom edge, and the bottle almost fills the full height.

A has no collisions, but its hierarchy is broken. The body copy is set almost as large as the headline and dominates the lower left, while the CTA button, 'Ships late June' and the legal text shrink to an illegible cluster on the right. The 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow is gone, and the logo is tiny. B is unusable: the last headline lines run into the body copy, the orange divider strikes through 'Smoked Rosemary', and the logo crowds the header band. These collisions outweigh its otherwise reasonable CTA prominence.

A re-wraps the headline into four large, centred lines that fill the portrait canvas, with the dark CTA clearly below it, so the hierarchy and brand feel survive. Its flaw is vertical imbalance: about 170px of space above the headline but only about 50px below the CTA, so the group sits low and the button is crowded toward the bottom edge. B leaves the whole bottom ~45% of the canvas as dead orange because the block sits above centre. Its two-line headline runs almost to the side edges with thin margins, and the CTA is jammed close under the headline, so it reads like the landscape layout pasted in rather than rearranged for the new shape.

A has a clean shared left edge and a logical order (logo, headline, subcopy, pills, CTA), but the headline leaves 'here' orphaned on its own line and the right ~40% of the canvas is empty apart from the peach circle, so the layout is lopsided. B's headline is oversized and runs almost to the right edge, and its left edge doesn't line up with the logo or subcopy. B's CTA floats on the right between the subcopy and the pills, the pills sit stranded below it, and the reading order and grouping are jumbled.

A is the better resize. It uses a sensible left-to-right banner structure: headline and tagline on the left, the date block in the middle, and the chips and a prominent RSVP button on the right. Its flaws are that the logo is jammed into the top-left corner over the circle, the can floats on its own above the date, the 'missing asset' placeholder is clipped at the right, and the legal line nearly touches the bottom edge. B demotes the RSVP CTA to a chip the same size as the badges, so the call to action is buried. It also wraps the tagline into a narrow five-line column, splits the date from the time with a large gap, crams the tiny legal text and the placeholder into the right corner, and lets the oversized two-line headline compete with everything, so the reading order is jumbled.

A is broken in several places. The book cover collides with the Inkwell & Lantern logo and clips its 'I'. The 'See the Schedule' button runs off the bottom edge. The fine print is jammed against the edge on top of confetti, and the whole card is cramped with no margins. B has a clean split: the book sits on the confetti on the left and the card on the right holds a strong headline, body copy and the CTA. Its flaws are a tiny, illegible logo, a small book cover floating with no clear anchor, the card running flush to the right and bottom edges, and fine print that competes beside the CTA.

A has a strong headline and CTA, but the plan cards are tiny and their labels can't be read. The cards are also out of order (6, 80, 48), and the subtitle and legal copy are crammed into a right-hand column that runs to the bottom edge. B is broken: the orphaned word 'week' collides with the subtitle, the card panels are cut off so the cream '48 / per year' sits on a light background and almost disappears, and the headline is too small to lead the layout.

A: the GLACIER logo now sits on the big teal circle, and the circle swallows the top of the product. The legal line floats mid-bottom on top of the light-blue circle, leaving a dead band beneath it. The product is shrunk and the composition looks pushed toward the top. B: the hierarchy and vertical order are clean, the product is larger and the legal text is at the bottom without overlap. However, the teal circle is shrunk into a floating disc that butts against the can's right green dot. Neither circle bleeds off the edge as in the original, which weakens the brand feel.

A reads well left to right with a strong headline and a big CTA, but it is cramped. The bottle cap touches the top edge, the headline's 'z' nearly runs into the overlapping corner circles, the CTA sits tight to the right edge, and the 3-line body copy is crowded. B's SOLSTICE logo is tiny and almost touches the bottle cap, and the body copy and CTA label are too small to read at banner size. Its small, centred content block also leaves a lot of empty space, so the hierarchy is weak.

A has severe collisions. The headline's last line sits on top of the body copy, the orange divider strikes through 'Smoked Rosemary', and the eyebrow crowds the logo, so the main message can't be read. B has no collisions and a readable headline, but the 'Reserve a Case' CTA has shrunk to an unreadable chip while the body copy is huge, which turns the hierarchy upside down. The eyebrow is missing, and the legal text and 'Ships late June' are illegibly small.

A squeezes the headline into two wide lines that nearly touch the left and right edges, and puts the whole text-and-button group in the upper middle. That leaves almost half the canvas below the CTA (the 'See the Flavours' button) as empty orange, which is lopsided and looks like a reused banner layout. B rewraps the headline into four large lines that suit the taller format and keeps the CTA clearly below it with good margins. Its only flaw is that the space above the headline is somewhat bigger than the space below the button, so the content sits slightly low.

A: the headline starts at x≈64 while the brand, subhead and chips start at x≈76, so the left edges don't line up, and the headline runs to about 30px from the right edge. The CTA floats mid-right above the chips, which breaks the reading order and the grouping. The small pink circle in the corner looks arbitrary. B: one clean left edge and a logical order from brand to headline, subhead, chips and CTA. But 'here' is orphaned on its own line, and the right half is mostly dead space apart from the bottom circle, which makes the layout lopsided.

A is jumbled: the RSVP CTA has been shrunk to the size of the FREE ENTRY/ALL AGES/TASTINGS pills, so it no longer stands out. The italic tagline is wrapped into a narrow five-line column, the URL and fine print are tiny, the partner mark is cropped to an unreadable sliver, and the reading order zigzags. B has clear columns (title, date, then pills and a large RSVP button) and keeps the hierarchy, but the can floats loosely beside the logo, the 'missing asset' placeholder box is prominent at the right, and the right side is left with uneven empty space.

A is a workable banner: the card on the right has a strong headline and a clear CTA, and the book sits on the confetti at left. But the Inkwell & Lantern logo is shrunk to an almost unreadable size and jammed into the card's top-left corner. The book cover is also small, the fine print is nearly as big as the body copy and crowds the CTA, and the card sits close to the canvas edges. B is broken: the book cover overlaps the logo and clips the 'I' of 'INKWELL'. Its CTA button runs off the bottom-left edge of the canvas, the fine print is tiny and crammed against the button and the confetti, and the widely spaced eyebrow line competes with the headline.

A has clear collisions: the headline's second line 'week' sits on top of the subtitle, and the legal text is crammed directly under it. The YEARLY card's '48' and 'per year' spill out of the dark card onto the light background, where they are almost invisible. B has a strong headline and a prominent CTA, but its price cards are shrunk to postage stamps with unreadable labels, and the plans are reordered (6, 80, 48), so YEARLY no longer sits in the centre. The subtitle and legal copy are squeezed against the right edge at an illegible size, but B at least has no collisions.

A keeps the original's layering, with the green circle tucked behind the bag and the olive circle at the bottom left, and it fills the tall canvas. Its headline is big and dominant, but it wraps so that 'fizz' sits alone on the second line, and the CTA is jammed close under the headline. B shrinks the CITRINE logo and the 'Find a Store' button text until they are hard to read, and the headline is noticeably smaller. It also leaves a dead gap between the bag and the headline and moves the green circle to a loose spot in the bottom right, which makes the lower third feel arbitrary and weakens fidelity to the original.

A reads left to right with the serif headline clearly dominant, but the rotated 'LONGEST DAY SALE' badge sits jammed against the bottom-left edge, the product can is shrunk so small it no longer matters, and the legal copy under the CTA is nearly as big as the button label and wraps awkwardly. B has broken hierarchy: the headline is tiny, about the size of the fine print, while the badge and CTA overpower it. The product is cut off at the left edge, the SOLSTICE wordmark collides with the can's label and becomes 'SOLSTI CE', and a large empty area sits between the copy and the CTA.

A: the GLACIER wordmark floats centred over nothing and does not line up with the headline's left edge. The can circle nearly touches the top and bottom of the canvas. The badge and CTA cluster on the right sits low and lines up with neither the copy block nor the image, so the layout feels arbitrary. B: GLACIER, the one-line headline, the body copy and the badges share a clean left edge, and the CTA on the right reads well as a banner. Its flaws: the body copy leaves an orphaned 'and bottles.', the badges are jammed against the bottom edge and cut off from the CTA, and the can's 'SOLSTICE' label is unreadably small in both.

A breaks the original's centred composition. The headline sits off-centre, to the right, and wraps badly, leaving 'sunshine.' alone on the second line. The CTA is pushed hard left on a different axis from the headline, and the LIMITED badge drifts to the right of the button as a separate oversized fragment, so nothing shares an edge. B keeps the centred headline with a balanced two-line break and keeps the original's badge-plus-CTA grouping. Its flaws: the headline is crammed near the top edge while a dead band of space sits below the button, and the badge-plus-button cluster is slightly off the headline's centre axis, the same off-centre placement as the original.

A shrinks the CITRINE wordmark and the 'Find a Store' label until they are hard to read, and leaves a large dead gap between the bag and the headline. It also pulls both circles fully inside the canvas so they float in the bottom third instead of bleeding off the edges as in the original. B keeps the original's bleeding circles, a readable CTA and a strong headline hierarchy, but the headline breaks badly and leaves 'fizz' alone on its own line. The olive circle also crowds the bottom-left corner, so B needs polish before it ships.

A: the headline is set tiny and loses to the oversized red badge and the CTA. The can is pushed against the left edge and its 'SOLSTICE' label spills past the can body. The standalone sun logo is gone, and the legal text is almost the same size as the headline. B: the headline is large and clearly leads, and the logo survives, but the 'LONGEST DAY SALE' banner is cut off at the bottom edge and sits over the planet circle. The can is shrunk to an icon, and the legal copy is crammed under the CTA and runs to the canvas edge.

A reads left to right, with the can, then a one-line headline and body, then the CTA at the right, but the badge row is jammed against the bottom edge and the body copy wraps to leave 'and bottles.' dangling. B's GLACIER logo is centred and floats off the headline's left edge. Its two-line headline eats the height, pushing the body copy and the CTA against the bottom edge, and the badge/CTA stack sits isolated at the right with an awkward gap between the columns.

A keeps the original centred headline and the LIMITED badge + CTA group. Its flaws: the headline sits only about 30px from the top while the bottom third is empty, and the CTA group is still off the headline's axis, as in the original. B breaks the alignment: the headline is pushed right of centre and its last line is a single word, 'sunshine.'. The CTA is jammed toward the left edge on a different axis, and the LIMITED badge is oversized and floats to the right of the button, separated from it, so the layout looks arbitrary.

A works as a left-to-right banner (copy, then bottle, then CTA) and keeps the bottle a sensible size. Its flaws: the Solstice logo is tiny and sits faintly on a background circle, the sale ribbon is jammed against the headline, and the left text block is cramped while the CTA floats alone on the right. B gives the headline strong prominence but sets it almost on the bottom edge. It also shrinks the bottle to a trivial thumbnail crammed in the top-right corner, leaves the ribbon floating in the middle unattached to anything, and stacks the subcopy, CTA and legal text tightly in a right column that runs to the bottom edge.

A keeps a strong, large two-line headline and a prominent CTA, but the alignment is mixed. GROVE is centred, the headline and body are left-aligned, and the pills and CTA are pushed right. The two pills almost touch, which makes the lower block look ragged. B shrinks the headline and CTA to weak sizes and squeezes the copy into a wide measure that leaves 'bottles.' as an orphan. It also drops the tilted Free Delivery badge into the pill row, where it looks like clutter, and leaves about 140px of dead space at the bottom while the text block sits cramped mid-canvas.

A keeps the original's centred hierarchy and brand intact, but it is basically the banner pasted into a square. The block sits high, leaving about 270px of dead orange below the CTA against about 190px above, so the layout feels top-heavy and unplanned. B does rearrange for the square, but the headline is so big that it crowds out everything else. The subcopy is squeezed into a centre-aligned 3-line rag ending in the fragment 'four flavours.', and it sits awkwardly beside the CTA in a bottom row whose edges (about 95px and 698px) don't line up with the headline column. That bottom row is cramped and looks off-grid.

A has a clean top-to-bottom stack with nothing colliding, but 'WEEKEND ONLY' has dropped below the body copy, so the eyebrow label now comes after the text it introduces. The body wraps badly and leaves 'sparkling.' alone on its own line, and the headline sits partly over the circle. B is unusable: the bottle sits on top of '20% off', the 'COLD BREW' label crowds into the headline, and the bottle covers 'case of' in the body copy. B also leaves the bottom third of the canvas empty below the CTA.

A: the bottom edge of the canvas cuts off the phone illustration and its backing circle. The 'Online Only' badge is stacked under 'Try It' at nearly the same size, so the two compete as focal points, and there is a large empty band below the subhead in the lower middle. B: the phone is fully visible and the 'Try It' button is clearly the strongest action, but the button and the tilted badge sit tight against the bottom edge, the backing circle is cropped, and the right-hand cluster feels cramped compared with the airy left side.

A keeps the original order: product circle on the left, then a headline, subhead and CTA stack that shares one left edge. Its flaws are small: the headline nearly touches the right edge and the large circle crowds the top and bottom margins. B breaks the grouping. The headline is alone on the left with nothing under it, the 'Try It' button runs into the bottom of the product circle, and 'Out now.' is pushed out to the side of the button with no connection to the headline. That leaves an empty left-bottom area and a crowded right cluster.

A is mostly a shrunk copy of the original with almost no rearranging. The pill tags and the URL become very small, and about 150px of the bottom is dead space with only the stray asset box in it. B is worse because of collisions: the line '6:00 pm… Pier 9' runs into the can and its green dots, and the subtitle's second line sits right on top of 'Saturday 21 June' with no gap. B also crams the info block close to the RSVP button and still leaves a large empty bottom third.

A has a strong, dominant headline, but the can is shrunk to a tiny icon jammed in the top-right corner on the circle, which makes the key product image unimportant. The sale ribbon floats on its own in the middle, and the legal text is as large as the subcopy, crammed into a crowded right column. B keeps the can as the central visual and reads left to right from message to product to CTA. Its weaknesses are a tiny logo pushed into the top-left corner, a tilted ribbon nearly touching the logo and headline, and a cramped left text block pressed against the edge.

A keeps a clean left edge, but the headline is shrunk to a single small line, about 140px of dead space sits at the bottom, and the tilted FREE DELIVERY badge has been moved down into the chip row, where it looks like a stray third chip. B keeps the headline larger and the badge in its original top-right spot, giving better hierarchy and fidelity, but it uses three axes at once: GROVE is centered, the headline and body are left-aligned, and the chips and CTA are pushed right. The two chips almost touch, and the chip row is jammed under the body copy.

A actually reworks the layout for the square: the headline is reset as a large four-line stack that fills the canvas. But the bottom row is weak. The subcopy is a small, centred, ragged three-line block, the CTA pill sits off to its right, and that pair breaks the headline's centred axis and crowds the bottom edge. B keeps the original centred stack unchanged, but the headline is too small for the square and the whole group sits high (about 190px above, 270px below), leaving a large empty orange area at the bottom. It reads as the banner dropped onto a bigger canvas, not a redesign.

A: the bottle sits on top of the body copy, covering 'case of', and it crowds right up against '20% off'. That is a clear collision. The bottom quarter of the canvas is also left as dead space under the CTA. B: nothing overlaps and it uses the tall format well. However, the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow has moved below the body copy, so the reading order is wrong. The left-aligned text clashes with the centred bottle and CTA, and 'sparkling.' is left alone on its own line.

A: the headline and CTA are large and the hierarchy is clear, but the CTA and ONLINE ONLY badge sit in a staircase jammed into the bottom-right corner (about 12px from the bottom and right edges), with the badge crowding the button. B reads well left to right, but the phone runs off the top and bottom edges and is cropped. The tilted badge is stacked directly under Try It in the same dark pill style, so it looks like a second competing button, and there is a large dead gap between the copy and the CTA column.

A breaks up the design. The 'Out now.' subline is moved off the headline and stuck beside the CTA, and the Try It button is jammed against the bottom of the product circle. The headline floats alone on the left above a large dead area, so the layout looks like scattered pieces. B keeps the original order: the product circle sits on the left and headline, subline and CTA form one left-aligned block on the right. Its flaws are small: the headline nearly touches the right edge, and the circle crowds the left, top and bottom edges.

A has a clear collision: the venue line '…Pier 9' runs into the tilted can graphic. 'Saturday 21 June' is jammed right under the subtitle's second line with no gap, and the subtitle wraps to an orphaned 'of the year'. B keeps the original's spacing and has no collisions, but it is mostly a scaled-down copy. The pill badges and URL text are small, the bottom third is dead space around the stray missing-asset box, and the big circle crowds the top-left behind the logo.

A reads properly left to right: can-in-circle, brand plus headline, body copy with badges, then a prominent CTA on the right. Its flaws are small: the body copy is small, the badges sit tight under the copy and the can icon is tiny. B is broken: the green circle is cut off at the left edge and split from the can, which floats on its own at the right. The SOLSTICE wordmark has dropped below the headline, the CTA has shrunk to badge size and is buried in the pill row, the body copy is illegibly small, and the right third is empty.

A reads clearly from left to right as brand, headline, then CTA, with the headline on one line. Its flaws: the phone is cropped by the top and bottom of the canvas, the CTA pill nearly touches both edges and squeezes its label, and the subhead and badges sit a little loose. In B, SOLSTICE floats on its own to the left of the headline, and the two-line headline is cramped. The subhead is tiny, and the BACK BY DEMAND badge is as big as the CTA and stacked right on top of it, which muddles the hierarchy. SUMMER ONLY is stranded in the right corner, and there is dead space between the phone and the text.

A reflows the design properly for the tall format: the product sits inside the lavender circle at the top, with a left-aligned stack below (kicker, headline, subcopy, CTA) and a clear hierarchy. Its flaws: the product is a little small inside the circle, the centered circle doesn't share an edge with the left-aligned text, and there's a dead gap between the CTA and the legal line. B's oversized '20% off' runs almost to the right edge and sits on a circle cropped at the top-right that no longer frames the product. 'WEEKEND ONLY' is crammed against the top edge, the legal line is nearly as large as the subcopy, and the product floats alone in the lower half, so the layout is top-heavy and cramped.

A: the bottle is the clear product hero and the headline, NEW badge and CTA sit together in one left-aligned column, but the bottle runs out past the bottom of its cream circle, the bottom ~200px of the canvas is empty, and the headline's 'Orange' comes close to the right edge. B: the bottle shrinks to a small thumbnail jammed into the top-left corner with a stray ghost circle clipped behind it; the NEW pill is blown up to nearly CTA size and competes with it; and the right-aligned buttons don't share an edge with the left-aligned headline, so the grid looks arbitrary and the bottom feels crowded.

A: The legal line runs straight into the placeholder image box. The phone overlaps that box and crowds the TASTINGS pill. The logo is shrunk to a tiny mark wedged inside the corner circle, and the headline is weak for the banner. B: It reads cleanly left to right and nothing collides. The large headline sits over the circle, which matches the original, so the hierarchy is stronger. Its flaws: the headline hugs the left edge, '6 pm' is indented out of line with the date, and the middle column is cramped, with the legal text jammed against the bottom edge.

A: the NEW VIDEO pill is clipped at the right canvas edge. The 'marathons' line almost touches the top of the lime circle, which reads as a collision. The headline is undersized for the format, and a dead band of space sits between the circle and 'Full review inside.' B: the headline is bigger and stronger, with a clean top row of logo and badge. However, the logo is shrunk, the shoe pokes past the left edge of the circle, and 'Full review inside.' is jammed between the circle bottom and the canvas edge.

A breaks the hero apart: the empty green circle is cut off at the left edge while the can floats alone at the far right. The SOLSTICE wordmark sits below the headline, the CTA is shrunk into a small pill and placed first in the badge row, and the body copy is tiny and illegible. B is a proper left-to-right leaderboard: the can stays in its circle, the brand sits above the headline, then the copy and badges, with a prominent CTA on the right. It only needs polish: the badges sit tight under the body copy, and the copy is small for the format.

A: the SOLSTICE wordmark sits awkwardly beside the top of the headline instead of above it, and there is a dead gap between the phone and the text. The 'Back by Demand' badge is as big as the CTA and sits directly on top of it, so the CTA is buried. The subcopy is tiny and the right ~180px of the banner is empty. B: it reads left to right with the logo, a single-line headline, then badges and the CTA. However, the phone is cropped top and bottom, the CTA is jammed against the right edge with its label crowding the pill, and the subcopy floats above the badges.

A places the lavender circle behind 'WEEKEND ONLY' and '20% off', so the decorative shape collides with the headline. The headline runs almost to the right edge, the CTA is oversized, and the can is left floating low with dead space around it, so it reads as a scaled-up stack rather than a layout made for this format. B is a clean top-to-bottom story layout: the can sits in its circle with a clear hierarchy below it. Its flaws are that the CTA and footer start at x≈20 while the copy starts at x≈35, and there is a slightly empty gap above the small footer.

A: the bottle is shrunk into a cramped top-left corner, its cap nearly touches the top edge, and a stray translucent circle overlaps it. The NEW badge and Try It button are right-aligned, so they don't share the headline's left edge, and the NEW pill is almost as large as the CTA, so the hierarchy competes. The bottom-left is a dead area. B: the bottle is a strong hero and the text column is cleanly left-aligned with good hierarchy. However, everything sits in the top two-thirds, leaving a large empty band at the bottom, and the headline runs close to the right edge.

A turns the design into a left-to-right banner. The large 'Sunset Sessions' headline clearly leads, and the logo, headline and subtitle stack together on the left. Its flaws: the middle column is cramped, with the date jammed near the top edge and the legal text squeezed under the URL. The time line is indented slightly from the date, so they don't share an edge. The grey placeholder box sits isolated at the far right. B is worse. Its logo is tiny and stuck in the corner over the circle, and 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' is left-aligned while the headline below it is centred. The 'TASTINGS' chip runs into the phone, and the legal line runs into the placeholder box at the bottom right, which also nearly touches the canvas edge. The headline is smaller, so the hierarchy is weaker.

A rebuilds the layout properly for the tall format. The logo and NEW VIDEO badge share the top row, the headline is big and left-aligned, and the shoe circle sits below it. Its flaws are small: the circle crowds 'Full review inside.', and that line sits tight to the bottom edge. B's NEW VIDEO badge is clipped at the right edge of the canvas. Its headline is smaller and 'marathons' almost touches the circle, while a large empty band sits below the small closing line, so the spacing is cramped at the top and dead at the bottom.
